Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a closed linear subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). By the orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) every $x\in H$ has a unique representation

$$x=P_Mx+(x-P_Mx),\qquad P_Mx\in M,\quad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp ,$$

and the **Hilbert orthogonal projection onto $M$** is the map

$$P_M:H\longrightarrow M\subseteq H,\qquad x\longmapsto P_Mx ,$$

assigning to $x$ its unique $M$-component. Its defining properties are therefore

$$P_Mx\in M,\qquad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp\qquad(x\in H),$$

which characterise $P_M$ uniquely: a map with these defining properties must agree with the $M$-component of the unique decomposition of each $x$.

**Agreement with the finite-dimensional projection.** If $V$ is a finite-dimensional inner-product space and $W\subseteq V$ a subspace, then [[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]] writes $V=W\oplus W^\perp$ and [[def-orthogonal-projection]] defines $P_Wv$ as the unique $W$-component of $v$; the defining properties displayed above are the same, so they define the same map on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.

**Range and kernel.** $P_Mx\in M$ for every $x$, and $P_Mm=m$ for $m\in M$ because $m=m+0$ with $0\in M^\perp$; conversely $P_Mx=0$ says exactly that $x=x-0\in M^\perp$. Hence the range of $P_M$ is $M$ and its kernel is $M^\perp$, and $P_M$ is the identity on $M$ and zero on $M^\perp$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

For this page, a Borel measure $\mu$ on a locally compact Hausdorff space is
**Radon** when $\mu(K)<\infty$ for every compact $K$, and, for every Borel
$E$ and every open $U$,
$$\mu(E)=\inf_{E\subseteq V\text{ open}}\mu(V),\qquad \mu(U)=\sup_{K\subseteq U\text{ compact}}\mu(K).$$
Cohn calls this convention regular. It does not assert compact inner
approximation for arbitrary Borel $E$.

A **regular Borel measure** here is a Radon measure $\mu$ for which every
Borel $E$ satisfies $\mu(E)=\sup_{K\subseteq E,\ K\text{ compact}}\mu(K)$,
with equality allowed at $+\infty$. Thus regularity strengthens the preceding
open-set formula; it is not being used as a synonym for Radon.

derivations.claim: [Strong continuity of tensoring with the identity] Let $M:=\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$. Strong convergence gives $\|Sx\|=\lim_{n}\|S_{n}x\|\le M\|x\|$ for every $x\in H$, so $\|S\|\le M$. For $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$ and $\varepsilon>0$, density [F1] gives a finite sum $z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|<\varepsilon/(4M+1)$. By linearity and the norm estimate [F1], $\|(S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I)\|\le M+\|S\|\le2M$, and hence $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))(z-z_{0})\|<\varepsilon/2$ for every $n$ (also when $M=0$, when the left side is zero). On the finite sum, [F1] gives $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))z_{0}\|\le\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|(S_{n}-S)u_{i}\|\,\|v_{i}\|\to0$. This is less than $\varepsilon/2$ for all large $n$, and the triangle inequality proves (c).

[Projection structure] For $B,C\in\Sigma$ one has $F(B)^{*}=(E(B)\otimes I)^{*}=E(B)^{*}\otimes I^{*}=E(B)\otimes I=F(B)$ and $F(B)^{2}=(E(B)\otimes I)(E(B)\otimes I)=E(B)^{2}\otimes I^{2}=E(B)\otimes I=F(B)$, so $F(B)$ is an orthogonal projection; moreover $F(B\cap C)=(E(B)E(C))\otimes I=(E(B)\otimes I)(E(C)\otimes I)=F(B)F(C)$, $F(\varnothing)=0\otimes I=0$ and $F(X)=I\otimes I=I$.

[Strong countable additivity] Let $(B_{n})$ be pairwise disjoint with union $B$. For finite $N$ the multiplicativity of step 1.2 and $F(B_{i})F(B_{j})=F(B_{i}\cap B_{j})=0$ for $i\ne j$ give $\sum_{n\le N}F(B_{n})=F(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})=E(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})\otimes I$. The orthogonal projections $E(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})$ are uniformly bounded by one and converge strongly to $E(B)$ by [F2], so step 1.1 gives $\sum_{n\le N}F(B_{n})\to F(B)$ strongly. Together with step 1.2, this proves (a), so $F$ is now a projection valued measure.

[Integral identity] Since step 2.1 proves that $F$ is a projection valued measure, the bounded PVM integral theorem [F3] applies to both $E$ and $F$. For a complex simple function $s=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\alpha_{k}\mathbf 1_{B_{k}}$ with $B_{k}\in\Sigma$ pairwise disjoint, linearity of $S\mapsto S\otimes I$ and of the integral [F1, F3] give $\Phi_{F}(s)=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}F(B_{k})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}(E(B_{k})\otimes I)=\bigl(\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}E(B_{k})\bigr)\otimes I=\Phi_{E}(s)\otimes I$. For bounded measurable $f$ choose simple $s_{n}$ with $\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\le 2^{-n}$ by partitioning a square containing the bounded range of $f$ into finitely many small squares; the norm bounds [F1, F3] give $\|\Phi_{F}(f)-\Phi_{F}(s_{n})\|\le\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$ and $\|\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I-\Phi_{E}(s_{n})\otimes I\|\le\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$, so uniqueness of limits yields $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I$, which is (b).

[Regularity on finite algebraic tensors] Assume $X$ locally compact Hausdorff with Borel $\sigma$-algebra and $E$ regular, and let $z_{0}=\kappa igl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i} igr)$. Put $C:=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|v_{i}\|^{2}$. If $m=0$ or $C=0$, then $z_{0}=0$, so $
u_{z_{0}}$ is the zero measure and is inner regular on every Borel set, taking the compact set $\varnothing$. Otherwise $m\ge1$ and $C>0$. For Borel $B$, $F(B)z_{0}=\kappa igl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}E(B)u_{i}\otimes v_{i} igr)$ by [F1], so the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the Euclidean pairing gives $
u_{z_{0}}(B):=\langle F(B)z_{0},z_{0}angle= igl\|\sum_{i}E(B)u_{i}\otimes v_{i} igr\|^{2}\le C\sum_{i}\langle E(B)u_{i},u_{i}angle$; also $
u_{z_{0}}(X)=\|z_{0}\|^{2}<+\infty$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, each finite measure $\langle E(\cdot)u_{i},u_{i}angle$ is regular by [F4], so there are compact $K_{i}\subseteq B$ with $\langle E(B\setminus K_{i})u_{i},u_{i}angle<\varepsilon/(mC)$; for the compact $K= igcup_{i}K_{i}$ one has $B\setminus K\subseteq B\setminus K_{i}$ and hence $
u_{z_{0}}(B)-
u_{z_{0}}(K)=
u_{z_{0}}(B\setminus K)\le C\sum_{i}\langle E(B\setminus K_{i})u_{i},u_{i}angle<\varepsilon$. Thus $
u_{z_{0}}$ is inner regular on Borel sets.

[Regularity on the completed product] Keep the hypotheses of step 3.2 and let $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$, $B$ Borel, $\varepsilon>0$; if $z=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $z
e0$ and choose $z_{0}=\kappa(\sum_{i}u_{i}\otimes v_{i})$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|\le\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ by [F1], then a compact $K\subseteq B$ with $
u_{z_{0}}(B\setminus K)\le\varepsilon/4$ by step 3.2. Since $F$ is projection valued by step 2.1, $
u_{z}(B)-
u_{z}(K)=\|F(B\setminus K)z\|^{2}\le igl(\|F(B\setminus K)(z-z_{0})\|+\|F(B\setminus K)z_{0}\| igr)^{2}\le igl(\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2+\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2 igr)^{2}=\varepsilon$, so $
u_{z}$ is inner regular on Borel sets; it is finite since $
u_{z}(X)=\|z\|^{2}<+\infty$. Inner regularity applied to the complement gives outer regularity: for Borel $E_{0}$ and $\eta>0$ choose compact $L\subseteq X\setminus E_{0}$ with $
u_{z}(X\setminus E_{0})-
u_{z}(L)<\eta$, so the open $V=X\setminus L$ contains $E_{0}$ and $
u_{z}(V)<
u_{z}(E_{0})+\eta$. Hence every $F_{z}$ is a regular Borel measure and $F$ is regular, which is (d).
[Assembly] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 3.1 proves (b), step 1.1 proves (c), and steps 3.2 and 4.1 prove (d).

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.2 computes F(∅)=0⊗I=0 and F(X)=I⊗I=I, the empty and full cases of the PVM clauses.

Step 1.1 permits M=0 and z=0 in its tensor-continuity estimate; step 1.2 gives 0 tensor I=0. Step 3.1 includes the zero simple function and zero bounded function. Step 3.2 explicitly handles m=0 or C=0, hence z_0=0 and the zero scalar measure; step 4.1 separately handles z=0.

boundaries.reason: No unit or singleton parameter is distinguished; the statement is uniform in the measurable space, the operators and the bounded function.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 permits zero limiting operators and M=0. Step 3.2 handles empty finite tensors and C=0 before dividing by mC. Step 4.1 handles the zero vector before its density/regularity estimates; no nonzero scalar mass is presumed.

boundaries.reason: X is an arbitrary measurable space; the locally compact case of clause (d) is topological and no interval endpoint occurs.

boundaries.evidence: The Axiom of Countable Choice is declared and used in step 1.1 through the density of the algebraic tensor product in the completion.

risk_review.notes: Read all seven steps and exact F1-F4 suppliers. Uniform operator bound 2M plus algebraic-tensor density proves strong extension, including M=0. Projection multiplicativity and strong disjoint sums establish a PVM before integrating; uniform simple approximation proves the bounded integral identity. Finite-tensor scalar measures are dominated by a finite sum of regular measures; compact unions and density give Borel inner regularity, and finite total mass gives outer regularity by complements. Empty tensors, zero vector and C=0 cases are covered. Countable Choice is carried from tensor/PVM suppliers. No unbounded tensor domain or physical assertion is inferred. Reader/refuter raise no finding here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with $H\widehat\otimes K$ their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). A **product vector** means an elementary tensor $v\otimes u$ with $v\in H$ and $u\in K$. Then for every $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable index set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq H$ and $(u_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq K$, and numbers $s_r>0$ with

$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r\qquad\text{(norm convergence in }H\widehat\otimes K),$$

and $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. The $s_r$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of $CC^*$, where $C:\overline{K_0}\to H_0$ is the linear coefficient operator on countable closed factor supports of $\Psi$, defined below; if $J$ is infinite then $s_r\to0$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ has $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector. No assertion about separability of mixed density operators is made here.

For clarity, choose finite algebraic tensors converging to $\Psi$ and let $H_0\subseteq H$, $K_0\subseteq K$ be the closed spans of their factor vectors. These supports have finite/countable orthonormal bases, and $\Psi\in H_0\widehat\otimes K_0$. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{K_0}$ consists of symbols $\bar z$, with $a\bar z:=\overline{\bar a z}$ and $\langle\bar z,\bar w\rangle_{\overline{K_0}}:=\langle w,z\rangle_{K_0}$. For an orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $K_0$, write $\Psi=\sum_jh_j\otimes f_j$ and set $C\bar f_j=h_j$, extending linearly and continuously. The positive singular values and the nonzero spectrum of $CC^*$ are independent of these supports and bases, as the reduced-state identity proved below shows.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],
   [[def-metric-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $\rho\in D(H)$ be a density operator ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). Let
$$(\lambda_n)_{n\in J},\qquad J\ \text{a finite initial segment of}\ \mathbb N\ \text{or all of}\ \mathbb N,$$
be the positive eigenvalues of $\rho$ listed with multiplicity, so that $\rho=\sum_{n\in J}\lambda_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ for an orthonormal family $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ of eigenvectors, $\rho u_n=\lambda_nu_n$ ([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]). Then:

(a) $\lambda_n>0$ for every $n\in J$, $\sum_{n\in J}\lambda_n=1$, and $\lambda_n\le1$ for every $n\in J$.

(b) $\rho^{2}$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator, and its positive eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are exactly the numbers $\lambda_n^{2}$ with $n\in J$; consequently
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})=\sum_{n\in J}\lambda_n^{2}\in(0,1].$$

(c) The following four statements are equivalent: (i) $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})=1$; (ii) $J=\{n_0\}$ for a single index $n_0$ and $\lambda_{n_0}=1$; (iii) $\rho$ is a pure state; (iv) $\rho^{2}=\rho$.

(d) If $\rho$ is not pure, then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})<1$ and $J$ contains at least two indices, so that $\rho$ has at least two positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Adopt the declared composite model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] with
subsystems $A,B$, assigned spaces $H,K$ and composite space
$H\widehat\otimes K$, the state postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the state space
$D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the framework
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
partial-trace and tensor construction results. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.

**(a) Reduced preparations.** For a preparation $\rho\in
D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the declared composite, the **reduced preparation
of subsystem $A$** is
$$\rho_{A}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),$$
the image of $\rho$ under the partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a), characterized by
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(X\otimes I_{K})\bigr) \qquad\text{for every bounded }X\in\mathcal B(H);$$
the **reduced preparation of subsystem $B$** is
$\rho_{B}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$, characterized by
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes Y))$ for
every bounded $Y\in\mathcal B(K)$. By clause (b) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] the partial trace maps density
operators to density operators and is trace preserving, so $\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho_{B}$ are states of the respective subsystems in the sense of the state
space of the framework.

**(b) Affineness and continuity.** The maps $\rho\mapsto\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho\mapsto\rho_{B}$ are affine and continuous in the trace norm:
$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ is linear and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T\|_{1}\le\|T\|_{1}$
by clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]], with the
trace norm of [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. In
particular the reduction of a statistical mixture
$\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of composite preparations is
the corresponding mixture $\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{A,n}$ of the reduced
preparations.

**(c) Product preparations reduce to their factors.** If
$\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is a
product preparation ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), then
$$T_{u\otimes v,\,u\otimes v}=T_{u,u}\otimes T_{v,v}$$
as bounded operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$, because both sides agree on
every elementary tensor $\kappa(x\otimes y)$ in the sense of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a) and $\kappa[H\odot K]$
is dense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c));
consequently
$$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u},\qquad \rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$$
by clause (c) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]. Thus a
product preparation is exactly a preparation whose reductions reconstruct it,
$\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, and whose reductions are pure.

**(d) Correlated and uncorrelated preparations.** A composite preparation
$\rho$ is called **uncorrelated** when $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ and
**correlated** otherwise; a pure preparation
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is called a product preparation when $\Psi$ is a product
vector and **non-product** otherwise
([[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clauses (a), (b)).
These are descriptive names for the displayed algebraic conditions; the
statistical reading of the distinction, including the failure of
factorization of local outcome laws for non-product pure preparations, is a
theorem of this page and is not assumed here.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix vocabulary: the subsystem states attached
to a composite preparation by the partial trace. The reduction is a
mathematical operation on the model description. It is not a dynamics, not an
interaction, not a measurement and not a physical discarding of subsystem $B$;
no disturbance of either subsystem and no empirical fact is asserted, and the
question whether a laboratory procedure prepares a state whose reduction is a
prescribed state is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The
physical reading of clause (a) — that the reduced preparation reproduces every
local outcome law of subsystem $A$ — is a theorem of this page and is not
assumed here.

Adopt the state and composition postulate (P1), the observable and probability
postulate (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate (P3) of the
framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
The following vocabulary is used by this page for a declared pair of
distinguishable subsystems.

**(a) Declared composite and its state space.** A **declared composite model**
is the assignment of two declared systems $A$ and $B$ of the massive-matter
sector, their assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces $H$ and $K$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i) and (iv),
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and the **composite assigned space**
$$H\widehat\otimes K,$$
the completed Hilbert tensor product of $H$ and $K$ with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], clause (iv) of P1). The
**state space of the declared composite** is $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$, the set of
density operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). A **preparation of the
composite** is an element of this set; the model's assignment of a state to a
preparation is the assignment of clause (iii) of P1, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(b) Product basis convention.** If $(e_{a})_{a\in\mathbf A}$ is a finite or
countable orthonormal basis of $H$ and $(f_{b})_{b\in\mathbf B}$ one of $K$,
then $(\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}))_{(a,b)\in\mathbf A\times\mathbf B}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (d)); every
$\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ has the expansion
$$\Psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}),\qquad c_{ab}\in\mathbb C,$$
converging in norm. A **product vector** is $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
$u\in H$, $v\in K$, and a **product preparation** is a state of the form
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$, $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Pure composite preparations are projectors $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ for unit vectors
$\Psi$ given by norm-convergent superpositions of product vectors as above.
General composite preparations are density operators on the completed product,
including statistical mixtures of pure composite preparations; these need not
factor. Superposition acts on vectors, while mixing acts on density operators
(P1 clauses (ii)-(iv)).

**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

**(d) Local effects.** A **local effect** of subsystem $A$ is a bounded
operator of the form $F\otimes I_{K}$ with $0\le F\le I_{H}$ in the
quadratic-form order; the map $F\mapsto F\otimes I_{K}$ is well defined by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a), and $F\otimes I_{K}$
is an effect on $H\widehat\otimes K$: it is bounded, self-adjoint
$((F\otimes I)^{*}=F^{*}\otimes I=F\otimes I)$, and it factors as
$$F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),\qquad I_{H}\otimes I_{K}-F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),$$
with the positive square roots of the continuous functional calculus
([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and
the product and adjoint rules of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (b), (c); hence
$0\le F\otimes I_{K}\le I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the quadratic-form order
([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).
Local effects of subsystem $B$ are defined in the same way.

**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates, defined only for outcomes with $p_a>0$,
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the reading of clause (iv) of P1 together
with clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) of P2 and clause (v) of P3 for a declared pair
of distinguishable subsystems. They add no physical assumption to those
postulates beyond the readings displayed. In particular: the subsystems are
distinguishable, so no exchange sector, symmetrization or exclusion statement
is introduced (those are separate assumptions of P6); no superselection
restriction or algebraic replacement of the tensor product is adopted; no
interaction, dynamics, disturbance of the other subsystem or correlation is
asserted; and whether a concrete laboratory arrangement realizes a declared
composite, a declared local readout or a declared local instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be arbitrary nonzero complex Hilbert spaces, with inner products linear in the first argument, and put $L=H\widehat\otimes K$ with the isometric inclusion $\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Write $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Set
$$\mathcal P=\{T_{\kappa(a\otimes b),\kappa(a\otimes b)}:\|a\|=\|b\|=1\},\qquad \mathcal S=\overline{\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P}^{\|\cdot\|_1},$$
with trace class as in [[def-trace-class-operator]], where the convex hull consists of finite convex combinations, and the closure is taken in the trace-class operators on $L$. For each unit $\Psi\in L$, let $P_\Psi=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$. Then
$$P_\Psi\in\mathcal S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)\text{ for some unit }a\in H,\ b\in K.$$

More precisely, let $\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\kappa(v_r\otimes u_r)$ be any finite or countably infinite positive Schmidt expansion from [[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]], and put $\lambda_r=s_r^2$. The number $m=\max_{r\in J}\lambda_r$ exists. Every pair of unit vectors $a,b$ satisfies $|\langle\Psi,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle|^2\le m$, with equality at a Schmidt pair whose weight is $m$. Every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\le m$, whereas $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1$. If $\Psi$ is non-product then $m<1$ and, for every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$,
$$\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge 1-m>0.$$
The factors need not be separable; only the support of the single tensor vector has a countable Schmidt expansion. These are mathematical trace pairings, with no measurement or Born-rule assumption.

derivations.claim: [Expansion and normalization] By [F1] there are $J$, $(v_{r})$, $(u_{r})$ and $s_{r}>0$ with $\Psi=\sum_{r}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ in norm and $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}=\|\Psi\|^{2}=1$; this is the expansion of (a).

[Finite truncations] Put $\Psi_{N}:=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ for an increasing sequence of finite subsets $J_{N}\uparrow J$. For bounded $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $N$ one has, using the tensor identity of [F1] on elementary tensors, $\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi_{N},\Psi_{N}\rangle=\sum_{r,r'\in J_{N}}s_{r}s_{r'}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r'}\rangle\langle u_{r},u_{r'}\rangle=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$ by orthonormality of $(u_{r})$; since $\Psi_{N}\to\Psi$, $\|X\otimes I_{K}\|\le\|X\|$ and $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}<\infty$, the sesquilinear form is continuous and the series converges absolutely, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$.

[Reduction identity] Let $S:=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{v_{r},v_{r}}$, a trace-class operator with $S\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}S=1$ by [F3] and absolute convergence. For bounded $X$, step 1.2 and [F2] give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$; taking $X=T_{w,w'}$ and using [F3] twice, $\langle\rho_{A}w,w'\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}T_{w,w'})=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle T_{w,w'}v_{r},v_{r}\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle v_{r},w'\rangle\langle w,v_{r}\rangle=\langle Sw,w'\rangle$ for all $w,w'\in H$, so $\rho_{A}=S$ by taking $w'=(\rho_{A}-S)w$ and using $\|(\rho_{A}-S)w\|^{2}=0$; interchanging the factors gives $\rho_{B}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{u_{r},u_{r}}$ with the same argument.

[Purity and product criterion] By [F1] and step 2.1, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{4}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero and exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; purity of $\rho_{A}$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ by [F4], and likewise for $\rho_{B}$. If exactly one $s_{r_{0}}$ is nonzero, then $s_{r_{0}}^{2}=1$ and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$ is a product vector, so $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ by [F5]; conversely for a product vector [F5] gives $\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$, which are pure by [F3] and [F4]. This is (b); its failure case, in which at least two $s_{r}$ are nonzero and both reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$ and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, is (c). Conversely, if $\rho=\rho_A\otimes\rho_B$, pair both operators with the unit product vector $q_r=\kappa(v_r\otimes u_r)$. The expansion gives $\langle\rho q_r,q_r\rangle=s_r^2$, while step 2.1 and the tensor action in [F1] give $\langle(\rho_A\otimes\rho_B)q_r,q_r\rangle=s_r^4$. Thus every positive $s_r^2$ equals its square and is one; their sum one forces exactly one coefficient. Finally [F6] identifies this product case exactly with separability, proving (vi); in the non-product case it gives entanglement and the stated strict trace-norm witness.

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 gives the expansion of (a) and step 2.1 its reduction formulae; step 3.1 establishes (b) and (c); only the declared composite, its pure preparations and the cited mathematics were used, which is the scope statement (d).

Step 2.1 takes the pairing against wʼ=(ρ_A−S)w and concludes from ‖(ρ_A−S)w‖²=0 that the two trace-class operators agree.
Step 3.1 treats the single-coefficient case s_{r0}=1 with its equivalences and the collapsed product form.
Step 3.1 treats the case of at least two nonzero coefficients, where both reduced preparations are mixed and ρ≠ρ_A⊗ρ_B.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement adopts the composite reading carrying AC for spectral readouts; step 1.1 uses only Countable Choice in tensor and Schmidt suppliers. No unbounded spectral construction is used in the deduction.
Step 3.1 derives from exactly one nonzero coefficient the purity of both reductions and the product form.
Step 3.1 derives from product form the purity identity tr ρ_A²=1 and the single nonzero coefficient.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a
measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) and let $E$ be a projection valued
measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).
Define, for $B\in\Sigma$,
$$F(B):=E(B)\otimes I_{K}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
the bounded tensor operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]
clause (a). Then:

(a) $F$ is a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on
$H\widehat\otimes K$;

(b) for every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb C$, writing
$\Phi_{F}(f)=\int f\,dF$ and $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ for the integrals of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], one has
$$\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I_{K};$$

(c) if $(S_{n})$ is a sequence of bounded operators on $H$ with
$\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and $S_{n}x\to Sx$ for every $x\in H$, then
$(S_{n}\otimes I_{K})z\to(S\otimes I_{K})z$ for every
$z\in H\widehat\otimes K$;

(d) if $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]),
$\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and $E$
regular in the sense of [[def-projection-valued-measure]], then $F$ is regular.

Clause (d) is what makes $F$ a regular projection valued measure on
$\mathbb R$ in the application to assigned sharp observables, so that the
converse direction of the spectral theorem supplies a self-adjoint operator
having $F$ as its spectral measure. No assertion is made about unbounded
operators in this lemma itself.
