preparation is the assignment of clause (iii) of P1, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(b) Product basis convention.** If $(e_{a})_{a\in\mathbf A}$ is a finite or
countable orthonormal basis of $H$ and $(f_{b})_{b\in\mathbf B}$ one of $K$,
then $(\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}))_{(a,b)\in\mathbf A\times\mathbf B}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (d)); every
$\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ has the expansion
$$\Psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}),\qquad c_{ab}\in\mathbb C,$$
converging in norm. A **product vector** is $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
$u\in H$, $v\in K$, and a **product preparation** is a state of the form
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$, $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Pure composite preparations are projectors $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ for unit vectors
$\Psi$ given by norm-convergent superpositions of product vectors as above.
General composite preparations are density operators on the completed product,
including statistical mixtures of pure composite preparations; these need not
factor. Superposition acts on vectors, while mixing acts on density operators
(P1 clauses (ii)-(iv)).

**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

**(d) Local effects.** A **local effect** of subsystem $A$ is a bounded
operator of the form $F\otimes I_{K}$ with $0\le F\le I_{H}$ in the
quadratic-form order; the map $F\mapsto F\otimes I_{K}$ is well defined by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a), and $F\otimes I_{K}$
is an effect on $H\widehat\otimes K$: it is bounded, self-adjoint
$((F\otimes I)^{*}=F^{*}\otimes I=F\otimes I)$, and it factors as
$$F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),\qquad I_{H}\otimes I_{K}-F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),$$
with the positive square roots of the continuous functional calculus
([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and
the product and adjoint rules of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (b), (c); hence
$0\le F\otimes I_{K}\le I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the quadratic-form order
([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).
Local effects of subsystem $B$ are defined in the same way.

**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates, defined only for outcomes with $p_a>0$,
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the reading of clause (iv) of P1 together
with clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) of P2 and clause (v) of P3 for a declared pair
of distinguishable subsystems. They add no physical assumption to those
postulates beyond the readings displayed. In particular: the subsystems are
distinguishable, so no exchange sector, symmetrization or exclusion statement
is introduced (those are separate assumptions of P6); no superselection
restriction or algebraic replacement of the tensor product is adopted; no
interaction, dynamics, disturbance of the other subsystem or correlation is
asserted; and whether a concrete laboratory arrangement realizes a declared
composite, a declared local readout or a declared local instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then for every bounded $B$

$$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. No cyclic permutation of unbounded operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has
   $$\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$$
   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   without assuming that $H$ has a Hilbert basis;
3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace
   norm: for trace-class $S,T$ and scalars $a,b$,
   $\operatorname{tr}(aS+bT)=a\operatorname{tr}(S)+b\operatorname{tr}(T)$ and
   $|\operatorname{tr}(T)|\le\|T\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],
   [[def-metric-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice is used only where the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators is invoked ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ with $\rho\ne\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Then:

(a) There is a unit vector $w\in H$ with $\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$.

(b) For the rank-one orthogonal projection $P:=T_{w,w}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), whose spectral projection-valued measure assigns $P$ to the Borel set $\{1\}$, the two scalar laws of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b) satisfy
$$\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\langle\rho w,w\rangle,\qquad \mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)=\langle\sigma w,w\rangle,$$
so the bounded sharp observable $P$ assigns different outcome probabilities to $\rho$ and $\sigma$.

(c) For every unit vector $w$ and every self-adjoint trace-class $T$ one has $|\operatorname{tr}(TT_{w,w})|\le\|T\|_1$; in particular $|\langle\rho w,w\rangle-\langle\sigma w,w\rangle|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 of the framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a declared ideal sharp measurement of a system with state space $D(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and let $\rho$ be a state. Then:

**(a) Outcome law.** For every outcome label $a$ the probability is $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, with $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; for the pure state of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$.

**(b) Conditional state and repeatability.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $a$ is the state $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=0$ for $b\ne a$. Immediate repetition of the same declared measurement therefore returns the same outcome with certainty:
$$\mathbb P(\text{second outcome }b\mid\text{first outcome }a)=\delta_{ab}.$$

**(c) Discarded outcomes.** The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ is a state and coincides with the outcome-weighted mixture of the conditional states,
$$\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a},$$
the series converging in trace norm; moreover $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ for every $a$ and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(\rho)P_{a}$. The conditional-vs-discarded distinction is therefore exactly the distinction between one selected branch $\rho_{a}$ and the mixture of all branches.

**(d) Compatible bounded quantities.** If $B$ is a bounded operator with $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. In particular, if the declared measurement is the spectral measurement of a bounded assigned sharp observable $A=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}$ (a finite or norm-convergent series with real $a_{a}$), then $A$ commutes with every $P_{a}$ and the mean of $A$ is unchanged by discarding the outcomes.

**(e) Loss of coherence.** If $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, then
$$\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v},\qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=0,$$
whereas for the coherent preparation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$: the discarded-outcome ensemble is the classical mixture of the branch states and carries no coherence between the ranges of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional on the adopted P3 and on the mathematical items cited; they do not assert that any laboratory apparatus realizes a declared ideal sharp measurement, do not select a unique recorded outcome, and do not describe the disturbance produced by an apparatus outside the declared class (clause (v) of P3). The identification of a device with a declared measurement is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a
measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) and let $E$ be a projection valued
measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).
Define, for $B\in\Sigma$,
$$F(B):=E(B)\otimes I_{K}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
the bounded tensor operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]
clause (a). Then:

(a) $F$ is a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on
$H\widehat\otimes K$;

(b) for every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb C$, writing
$\Phi_{F}(f)=\int f\,dF$ and $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ for the integrals of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], one has
$$\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I_{K};$$

(c) if $(S_{n})$ is a sequence of bounded operators on $H$ with
$\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and $S_{n}x\to Sx$ for every $x\in H$, then
$(S_{n}\otimes I_{K})z\to(S\otimes I_{K})z$ for every
$z\in H\widehat\otimes K$;

(d) if $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]),
$\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and $E$
regular in the sense of [[def-projection-valued-measure]], then $F$ is regular.

Clause (d) is what makes $F$ a regular projection valued measure on
$\mathbb R$ in the application to assigned sharp observables, so that the
converse direction of the spectral theorem supplies a self-adjoint operator
having $F$ as its spectral measure. No assertion is made about unbounded
operators in this lemma itself.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

derivations.claim: [Intertwining identity] Let $T$ be trace class on $H\widehat\otimes K$ and $X,Y$ bounded on $H$. For every bounded $Z$ on $H$, [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\bigl((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I)\bigr)Z\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I)(Z\otimes I)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(YZX\otimes I)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)(YZX)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)YZ\bigr)$ by [F3] and [F6]; since $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I))$ and $X(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)Y$ are trace-class operators with equal trace pairings against every bounded $Z$, they are equal by [F3].

[The extended family is a declared measurement] The operators $P_{a}\otimes I_{K}$ are orthogonal projections by [F6]; $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$ gives $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})(P_{b}\otimes I_{K})=(P_{a}P_{b})\otimes I_{K}=0$; and $\sum_{a\in A_{0}}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})=I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the strong sense, because the finite partial sums are $(\sum_{a\le N}P_{a})\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity and converge strongly to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ by [F6], the projections $\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}$ being uniformly bounded and converging strongly to $I_{H}$. Hence $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement of the composite.

[Local readout law] For every Borel $B$, [F1] gives $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}))$, and [F2] applied with the bounded operator $E_{A}(B)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}E_{A}(B))=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B)$ by [F1]; applying the same identity to $\rho'$ gives the case $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$, so this is (a).

[Determination of the reduced preparation] Suppose $\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$. By [F4] there is a unit $w$ with $\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle\ne\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$; declare the bounded self-adjoint operator $P:=T_{w,w}$ with unit $1$ as a bounded assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$. Its local readout $(P^{\mathrm{loc}},1)$ has, by step 1.3, the outcome law $\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle$, and likewise $\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(\{1\})=\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$; the two numbers differ, so some local readout law differs, which is (b).

[Conditional local measurement] By step 1.2 the family $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement of the composite, so [F5] gives $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a})$ by [F2], and the conditional state $\rho_{a}=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$. Step 1.1 with $X=Y=P_{a}$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\bigl((P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}$, hence $(\rho_{a})_{A}=P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}/p_{a}$; the conditional update of the composite reduces to the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$, which is the first part of (c).

[Discarded local measurement] The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)$ of [F5] has $A$-reduction $\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}$: apply $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ to the trace-norm convergent series termwise using step 1.1 and the trace-norm continuity of $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ from [F2]. For the $B$-reduction let $Y$ be bounded on $K$, enumerate the outcomes, and set $S_N=\sum_{a\le N}P_a$. Orthogonality and the strong resolution of the identity give $0\le S_N\le I_H$ and $S_N\to I_H$ strongly. By [F6], $S_N\otimes I_K\to I_H\otimes I_K$ strongly, and the tensor product rule gives $S_N\otimes Y=(S_N\otimes I_K)(I_H\otimes Y)\to I_H\otimes Y$ strongly with $\sup_N\|S_N\otimes Y\|\le\|Y\|$. The strong limit passes through this trace pairing by a finite-tail argument: [F7] and the rank-one trace identity in [F3] give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(S_N\otimes Y))=\sum_kw_k\langle(S_N\otimes Y)u_k,u_k\rangle$. For each $k$ the summand converges to $w_k\langle(I_H\otimes Y)u_k,u_k\rangle$, and its modulus is at most $w_k\|Y\|$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose a finite initial segment ending at $N_0$ whose omitted weights sum to less than $\varepsilon/(4\|Y\|)$ when $Y\ne0$; the tail of the difference from the limit is at most $2\|Y\|\sum_{k>N_0}w_k<\varepsilon/2$, while strong convergence on the finite segment makes that part less than $\varepsilon/2$ for all sufficiently large $N$; hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(S_N\otimes Y))\to\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I_H\otimes Y))$. The case $Y=0$ is immediate. Now let $\Phi_N(\rho)=\sum_{a\le N}(P_a\otimes I_K)\rho(P_a\otimes I_K)$. Trace-norm convergence in [F5] and the trace ideal bound give $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi_N(\rho)(I_H\otimes Y))\to\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)(I_H\otimes Y))$. For each finite $N$, cyclicity [F3] and the tensor rules [F6] give $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi_N(\rho)(I_H\otimes Y))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(S_N\otimes Y))$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)(I_H\otimes Y))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I_H\otimes Y))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_BY)$ by [F2]. Since the trace pairings against every bounded $Y$ determine a trace-class operator, $\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_B$. This completes (c); the exchanged-roles statement is the same argument with $H$ and $K$ interchanged.
[Assembly and scope] Step 1.3 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), steps 2.2 and 2.3 are (c), and (d) records that only P1, P2, P3 in their stated readings and the cited mathematics were used.

boundaries.evidence: Statement(c) normalizes the ideal measurement family to I_H on nonzero H, excluding an empty full outcome index. Empty partial sums in step 1.2 are zero projections and extend to zero under tensoring. For the empty Borel event, step 1.3 gives E_A(empty)=0 and equal zero probabilities.
Step 2.1 proves equal local laws for equal reduced preparations and step 2.2 distinguishes different reduced preparations, which is the zero and nonzero difference of the local laws.

boundaries.reason: No unit or singleton parameter is distinguished; the argument is uniform in the preparations and in the Borel set.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 holds for every preparation, including the maximally mixed reduced preparation, and for every Borel set, so no rank or degeneracy exclusion is needed.

boundaries.reason: The outcome space is the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ, which has no interval endpoints, and clause (a) holds for every Borel set.

boundaries.evidence: The local readout uses the spectral theorem through steps 1.3 and 2.1, and both the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are declared.
Step 2.1 shows that equal reduced preparations give equal local readout laws.
Step 2.2 shows that different reduced preparations differ in some local readout law.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with $H\widehat\otimes K$ their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). A **product vector** means an elementary tensor $v\otimes u$ with $v\in H$ and $u\in K$. Then for every $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable index set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq H$ and $(u_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq K$, and numbers $s_r>0$ with

$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r\qquad\text{(norm convergence in }H\widehat\otimes K),$$

and $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. The $s_r$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of $CC^*$, where $C:\overline{K_0}\to H_0$ is the linear coefficient operator on countable closed factor supports of $\Psi$, defined below; if $J$ is infinite then $s_r\to0$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ has $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector. No assertion about separability of mixed density operators is made here.

For clarity, choose finite algebraic tensors converging to $\Psi$ and let $H_0\subseteq H$, $K_0\subseteq K$ be the closed spans of their factor vectors. These supports have finite/countable orthonormal bases, and $\Psi\in H_0\widehat\otimes K_0$. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{K_0}$ consists of symbols $\bar z$, with $a\bar z:=\overline{\bar a z}$ and $\langle\bar z,\bar w\rangle_{\overline{K_0}}:=\langle w,z\rangle_{K_0}$. For an orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $K_0$, write $\Psi=\sum_jh_j\otimes f_j$ and set $C\bar f_j=h_j$, extending linearly and continuously. The positive singular values and the nonzero spectrum of $CC^*$ are independent of these supports and bases, as the reduced-state identity proved below shows.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The adopted composite
reading also carries the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for its
local spectral readouts; the Schmidt and partial-trace deductions below use
only Countable Choice. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ satisfy
$\|\Psi\|=1$, let
$$\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K),\qquad \rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),\qquad \rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$$
be the pure preparation of the declared composite and its two reduced
preparations. Then:

**(a) Schmidt expansion and reductions.** There are an at most countable index
set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq H$,
$(u_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq K$ and numbers $s_{r}>0$ with
$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\,\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})\quad\text{(norm convergence)},\qquad \sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}=1,$$
and the reduced preparations are given by the trace-norm convergent series
$$\rho_{A}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{v_{r},v_{r}},\qquad \rho_{B}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{u_{r},u_{r}} .$$
Moreover $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{4}$.

**(b) Purity and product criterion.** The following are equivalent:
(i) exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero; (ii) $\rho_{A}$ is pure, that is
$\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$; (iii) $\rho_{B}$ is pure;
(iv) $\Psi$ is a product vector, $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$; (v) $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$; (vi) $\rho$ is separable in the trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). In that case
$s_{r_{0}}=1$ at the unique nonzero index and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$,
$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ for $u=v_{r_{0}}$, $v=u_{r_{0}}$.

**(c) Non-product pure preparations.** If $\Psi$ is not a product vector, then
at least two coefficients $s_{r}$ are nonzero, $\rho_{A}$ and $\rho_{B}$ are
mixed, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$, and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$;
the pure preparation is entangled in the full trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). More precisely, if $m=\max_rs_r^2<1$, every separable $\sigma$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma\rho)\le m$ and $\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\ge1-m>0$.

**(d) Scope.** The statement concerns the declared composite, its pure
preparations and the reduced preparations of the factors. It asserts no
dynamics, no interaction, no measurement, no apparatus realization and no
empirical fact; and it concerns pure composite preparations only, mixed-state
separability being outside its scope.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],
   [[def-metric-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Assume AC. For a bounded self-adjoint operator $T$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space there is a unique isometric unital star-homomorphism $C(\sigma(T))\to\mathcal B(H)$, $f\mapsto f(T)$, sending the coordinate function $z$ to $T$, with range $C^*(I,T)$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: [Declared joint POVM] Let $(F_i)_{i=1}^{n}$ and $(F'_j)_{j=1}^{m}$ be finite local effect families with $\sum_iF_i=I_H$ and $\sum_jF'_j=I_K$. Define $G_{ij}:=F_i\otimes F'_j$. By [F5] the positive square roots exist, and the tensor adjoint and product rules [F3] give $G_{ij}=(F_i^{1/2}\otimes(F'_j)^{1/2})^{*}(F_i^{1/2}\otimes(F'_j)^{1/2})\ge0$. Bilinearity of bounded tensoring gives $\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}=(\sum_iF_i)\otimes(\sum_jF'_j)=I_H\otimes I_K$. Thus every $G_{ij}\le I$ and the family $(G_{ij})$ satisfies the finite-outcome requirements of P2 on the product outcome set; [F4] assigns the joint probabilities $p(i,j)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G_{ij})$. This is the joint law used in (a).

[Non-product case] Let $\Psi$ be non-product. By [F1] its norm-convergent Schmidt expansion has at least two positive coefficients; label two of them $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$ and put $P=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$, $P'=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$. Since $Pv_{r}=\delta_{r,1}v_{1}$ and $P'u_{r}=\delta_{r,2}u_{2}$ by the rank-one definition and orthonormality, [F3] gives $(P\otimes P')\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})=\delta_{r,1}\delta_{r,2}\kappa(v_{1}\otimes u_{2})=0$ for every $r$. Boundedness of $P\otimes P'$ passes this identity through the norm-convergent Schmidt expansion, so $(P\otimes P')\Psi=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes P'))=0$ by [F2]. The trace-norm expansions of the reduced preparations [F1], paired with the bounded projections, give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=s_{1}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P')=s_{2}^{2}$ by [F2]. Thus the marginal product exceeds the joint probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$. The two local measurements $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ are effect families by [F2], [F4], and their $(+,+)$ entry already proves nonfactorization.

[Product case] Let $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and let $F,F'$ be bounded effects. By [F5] and the tensor calculus [F3], the same square-root factorization as in step 1.1 shows $F\otimes F'\ge0$, and $I_H\otimes I_K-F\otimes F'=(I_H-F)\otimes I_K+F\otimes(I_K-F')\ge0$, since each term on the right factors as $R^{*}R$ using [F5] and [F3]. Thus $F\otimes F'$ is an effect. By [F2] and [F3], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(F\otimes F'))=\langle(F\otimes F')\Psi,\Psi\rangle_{\widehat\otimes}=\langle Fu,u\rangle_H\langle F'v,v\rangle_K=\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}F)\operatorname{tr}(T_{v,v}F')=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_AF)\operatorname{tr}(\rho_BF')$ by [F1]. For arbitrary $F,F'$, apply step 1.1 to the binary local families $(F,I_H-F)$ and $(F',I_K-F')$; it declares $F\otimes F'$ as their joint $(+,+)$ effect. For general finite outcome families, step 1.1 gives the corresponding declared joint probabilities and marginals, so they factorize. This is (a).

[Assembly and scope] Steps 2.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b); only the declared composite, its pure preparations and the cited mathematics were used, and no dynamics, apparatus or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (c).

Step 1.1 is the case of a single Schmidt coefficient, that is, s_{1}=1 and a product vector.

Square-root tensor factorizations prove product effects positive; I-F tensor Fprime decomposition proves the upper bound, and finite joint effects sum to I before assigning probabilities.
