citations.quote:
Adopt the state and composition postulate (P1), the observable and probability
postulate (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate (P3) of the
framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
The following vocabulary is used by this page for a declared pair of
distinguishable subsystems.

**(a) Declared composite and its state space.** A **declared composite model**
is the assignment of two declared systems $A$ and $B$ of the massive-matter
sector, their assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces $H$ and $K$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i) and (iv),
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and the **composite assigned space**
$$H\widehat\otimes K,$$
the completed Hilbert tensor product of $H$ and $K$ with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], clause (iv) of P1). The
**state space of the declared composite** is $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$, the set of
density operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). A **preparation of the
composite** is an element of this set; the model's assignment of a state to a
preparation is the assignment of clause (iii) of P1, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(b) Product basis convention.** If $(e_{a})_{a\in\mathbf A}$ is a finite or
countable orthonormal basis of $H$ and $(f_{b})_{b\in\mathbf B}$ one of $K$,
then $(\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}))_{(a,b)\in\mathbf A\times\mathbf B}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (d)); every
$\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ has the expansion
$$\Psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}),\qquad c_{ab}\in\mathbb C,$$
converging in norm. A **product vector** is $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
$u\in H$, $v\in K$, and a **product preparation** is a state of the form
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$, $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Pure composite preparations are projectors $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ for unit vectors
$\Psi$ given by norm-convergent superpositions of product vectors as above.
General composite preparations are density operators on the completed product,
including statistical mixtures of pure composite preparations; these need not
factor. Superposition acts on vectors, while mixing acts on density operators
(P1 clauses (ii)-(iv)).

**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

**(d) Local effects.** A **local effect** of subsystem $A$ is a bounded
operator of the form $F\otimes I_{K}$ with $0\le F\le I_{H}$ in the
quadratic-form order; the map $F\mapsto F\otimes I_{K}$ is well defined by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a), and $F\otimes I_{K}$
is an effect on $H\widehat\otimes K$: it is bounded, self-adjoint
$((F\otimes I)^{*}=F^{*}\otimes I=F\otimes I)$, and it factors as
$$F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),\qquad I_{H}\otimes I_{K}-F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),$$
with the positive square roots of the continuous functional calculus
([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and
the product and adjoint rules of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (b), (c); hence
$0\le F\otimes I_{K}\le I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the quadratic-form order
([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).
Local effects of subsystem $B$ are defined in the same way.

**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates, defined only for outcomes with $p_a>0$,
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the reading of clause (iv) of P1 together
with clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) of P2 and clause (v) of P3 for a declared pair
of distinguishable subsystems. They add no physical assumption to those
postulates beyond the readings displayed. In particular: the subsystems are
distinguishable, so no exchange sector, symmetrization or exclusion statement
is introduced (those are separate assumptions of P6); no superselection
restriction or algebraic replacement of the tensor product is adopted; no
interaction, dynamics, disturbance of the other subsystem or correlation is
asserted; and whether a concrete laboratory arrangement realizes a declared
composite, a declared local readout or a declared local instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a
measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) and let $E$ be a projection valued
measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).
Define, for $B\in\Sigma$,
$$F(B):=E(B)\otimes I_{K}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
the bounded tensor operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]
clause (a). Then:

(a) $F$ is a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on
$H\widehat\otimes K$;

(b) for every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb C$, writing
$\Phi_{F}(f)=\int f\,dF$ and $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ for the integrals of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], one has
$$\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I_{K};$$

(c) if $(S_{n})$ is a sequence of bounded operators on $H$ with
$\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and $S_{n}x\to Sx$ for every $x\in H$, then
$(S_{n}\otimes I_{K})z\to(S\otimes I_{K})z$ for every
$z\in H\widehat\otimes K$;

(d) if $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]),
$\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and $E$
regular in the sense of [[def-projection-valued-measure]], then $F$ is regular.

Clause (d) is what makes $F$ a regular projection valued measure on
$\mathbb R$ in the application to assigned sharp observables, so that the
converse direction of the spectral theorem supplies a self-adjoint operator
having $F$ as its spectral measure. No assertion is made about unbounded
operators in this lemma itself.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $H$ be the nonzero complex Hilbert space assigned to a declared system ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), and let $(M_{a})_{a\ge1}$ be a declared normalized countable Kraus family on $H$: bounded operators with
$$\sum_{a=1}^{N}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}\longrightarrow I\qquad\text{strongly as }N\to\infty .$$
Declare the countable instrument with outcome set $\{1,2,\dots\}$, effects $F_{a}:=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}$, outcome probabilities $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$, conditional updates $\rho_{a}:=M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$, and discarded-outcome map $\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\ge1}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d)). Then:

**(a) POVM and discarded ensemble.** Each $F_{a}$ is an effect, $0\le F_{a}\le I$; for every state $\rho$ one has $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; $\Phi$ is a positive trace-preserving linear map of the trace-class operators and maps states to states; and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$, a trace-norm convergent mixture of the conditional states.

**(b) Repeatability criterion.** The declared instrument is **repeatable**, i.e. for every state $\rho$ and every $a$ with $p_{a}>0$ an immediate repetition of the same declared instrument returns the outcome $a$ with probability $1$ and every $b\ne a$ with probability $0$, if and only if
$$M_{b}M_{a}=0\qquad\text{for all }a,b\text{ with }b\ne a .$$
Equivalently, $M_a^*F_aM_a=F_a$ for every $a$. If $H$ is finite-dimensional, this criterion also forces each $F_a$ to be an orthogonal projection; the projection condition is not imposed for general $H$.

**(c) Projective case.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})$ the Kraus family $M_{a}=P_{a}$ satisfies the criterion of (b) and is repeatable, in agreement with [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clause (b); a general normalized Kraus family need not satisfy it ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (c)).

**(d) Non-determination.** The effects $(F_{a})$ determine the outcome probabilities but not the conditional updates; the Kraus family is part of the declared instrument (clause (v) of P3, [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (b)).

**(e) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared countable instrument; they assert no apparatus realization, no outcome uniqueness and no empirical fact, and no claim is made that every positive trace-preserving map admits such a Kraus family ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]] clause (c)).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces, let $(M_a)_{a\ge1}$ be bounded operators on $K$ with $\sum_{a\le N}M_a^*M_a\to I_K$ strongly, and let $R$ be a trace-class operator on $H\widehat\otimes K$. In this statement, $R\ge0$ means that $R$ is self-adjoint and $\langle Rx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$, as in [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]. Then the series (when either factor is $\{0\}$, use the zero partial-trace maps $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_H:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(K)$; when both factors are nonzero, use the partial traces of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]])

$$\sum_{a\ge1}(I_H\otimes M_a)R(I_H\otimes M_a^*)$$

converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(R)$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(R)=\operatorname{tr}R$ and $\Phi(R)\ge0$ if $R\ge0$, and the reduced state on $H$ is unchanged:

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K\Phi(R)=\operatorname{Tr}_KR .$$

By symmetry, a local map $R\mapsto\sum_a(N_a\otimes I_K)R(N_a^*\otimes I_K)$ on the first factor also leaves $\operatorname{Tr}_HR$ fixed. Selective conditioning (one summand normalized by its nonzero trace) is not covered.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for a
declared composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned
spaces $H,K$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited suppliers. Let $\rho,\rho'\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be
preparations with reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$,
$\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ and
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$. Then:

**(a) Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of
subsystem $A$ with local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{A}\,E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B),$$
where $E_{A}$ is the spectral projection valued measure of $A$. In particular
the local statistics of subsystem $A$ depend on the composite preparation only
through its reduced preparation, and if $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$ then every local
readout law is the same in $\rho$ and in $\rho'$.

**(b) Determination of the reduced preparation.** Conversely, if
$\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$, then there are a bounded assigned sharp observable
$(P,1)$ of subsystem $A$ and a Borel set $B$ with
$\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)\ne\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)$: the
family of local readout laws of subsystem $A$ determines $\rho_{A}$ among the
preparations of the composite.

**(c) Ideal local measurement.** Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ be a declared
ideal sharp measurement of subsystem $A$
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (a)). Then $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})_{a\in A_{0}}$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement of the declared composite, its outcome probabilities in a
preparation $\rho$ are
$$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a}),$$
and for $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state
$\rho_{a}:=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ of the
composite has the reduced preparation
$$(\rho_{a})_{A}=\frac{P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
which is the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$ by $P_{a}$. The
discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$
has reduced preparations
$$\Phi(\rho)_{A}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a},\qquad \Phi(\rho)_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{B} .$$
The analogous statements hold with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the readings of the cited items and of the cited mathematics. They concern
the declared composite and its declared measurements; they assert no dynamics,
no interaction, no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes
and no empirical fact, and clause (c) is a statement about the declared ideal
Lueders instrument only, not about every laboratory procedure.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Adopt the declared composite model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] with
subsystems $A,B$, assigned spaces $H,K$ and composite space
$H\widehat\otimes K$, the state postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the state space
$D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the framework
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
partial-trace and tensor construction results. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.

**(a) Reduced preparations.** For a preparation $\rho\in
D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the declared composite, the **reduced preparation
of subsystem $A$** is
$$\rho_{A}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),$$
the image of $\rho$ under the partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a), characterized by
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(X\otimes I_{K})\bigr) \qquad\text{for every bounded }X\in\mathcal B(H);$$
the **reduced preparation of subsystem $B$** is
$\rho_{B}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$, characterized by
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes Y))$ for
every bounded $Y\in\mathcal B(K)$. By clause (b) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] the partial trace maps density
operators to density operators and is trace preserving, so $\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho_{B}$ are states of the respective subsystems in the sense of the state
space of the framework.

**(b) Affineness and continuity.** The maps $\rho\mapsto\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho\mapsto\rho_{B}$ are affine and continuous in the trace norm:
$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ is linear and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T\|_{1}\le\|T\|_{1}$
by clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]], with the
trace norm of [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. In
particular the reduction of a statistical mixture
$\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of composite preparations is
the corresponding mixture $\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{A,n}$ of the reduced
preparations.

**(c) Product preparations reduce to their factors.** If
$\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is a
product preparation ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), then
$$T_{u\otimes v,\,u\otimes v}=T_{u,u}\otimes T_{v,v}$$
as bounded operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$, because both sides agree on
every elementary tensor $\kappa(x\otimes y)$ in the sense of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a) and $\kappa[H\odot K]$
is dense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c));
consequently
$$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u},\qquad \rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$$
by clause (c) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]. Thus a
product preparation is exactly a preparation whose reductions reconstruct it,
$\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, and whose reductions are pure.

**(d) Correlated and uncorrelated preparations.** A composite preparation
$\rho$ is called **uncorrelated** when $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ and
**correlated** otherwise; a pure preparation
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is called a product preparation when $\Psi$ is a product
vector and **non-product** otherwise
([[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clauses (a), (b)).
These are descriptive names for the displayed algebraic conditions; the
statistical reading of the distinction, including the failure of
factorization of local outcome laws for non-product pure preparations, is a
theorem of this page and is not assumed here.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix vocabulary: the subsystem states attached
to a composite preparation by the partial trace. The reduction is a
mathematical operation on the model description. It is not a dynamics, not an
interaction, not a measurement and not a physical discarding of subsystem $B$;
no disturbance of either subsystem and no empirical fact is asserted, and the
question whether a laboratory procedure prepares a state whose reduction is a
prescribed state is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The
physical reading of clause (a) — that the reduced preparation reproduces every
local outcome law of subsystem $A$ — is a theorem of this page and is not
assumed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: [Extension and discarded map] By [F1] the family $(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})$ is a declared instrument of the composite with effects $I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$ and conditional states $\rho_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$; by [F2] its discarded-outcome map $\Phi$ is positive and trace preserving, so $\Phi(\rho)$ is a preparation of the composite; and re-indexing the doubly indexed family as a sequence $(N_{b})$ on $K$ with $\sum_{b\le N}N_{b}^{*}N_{b}\to I_{K}$ strongly, [F3] gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho=\rho_{A}$. This is (a) together with the first assertion of (b); likewise $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$ by [F5].

[No-signalling] Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable of $A$. By step 1.1 the state $\Phi(\rho)$ has reduced preparation $\rho_{A}$, so [F4] gives $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\Phi(\rho)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}E_{A}(B))=\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)$ for every Borel $B$: no local A-statistic changes under the discarded local instrument. This is (b).

[Conditional reductions] For each $a$ with $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state $\rho_{a}$ of [F2] satisfies $p_{a}\rho_{a}=\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\rho(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$, so by linearity and trace-norm continuity of $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ from [F5] one has $p_{a}(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\rho(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$. Summing over the positive-probability outcomes and using the trace-norm convergence of the discarded series from [F3] gives $\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{A}$ by step 1.1; the terms for zero-probability outcomes are zero contributions to $\Phi(\rho)$ and no conditional state is assigned to them. This is (c); the exchanged-roles form of (b) is the same argument with $H$ and $K$ interchanged.
[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 2.2 is (c), and (d) records that only the declared readings and the cited mathematics were used, with no causality or apparatus claim.

boundaries.evidence: The full Kraus family sums to I_K on nonzero K and cannot be empty. Individual R_a can be empty: then F_a=0 and p_a=0, their unnormalized sums vanish and the p_a>0 condition prevents defining a conditional state. Steps 1.1 and 2.2 retain only the zero contribution in discarded/weighted sums.
The conditional states are defined only for p_a>0 and step 2.2 averages them with the weights p_a, so outcomes of zero probability are excluded exactly as stated.
A single-outcome instrument is the special case of step 2.1, which never uses more than one outcome of the instrument at a time.
Step 2.2 covers conditional reductions that differ from ρ_A and average back to it, including projective and single-Kraus degenerate cases of the declared instrument.

risk_review.notes: Checked all four steps and grouped Kraus definition, normalized countable-Kraus theorem, local trace-preserving lemma and local-readout law. Enumeration preserves strong completeness for finite/countable total indices; finite families may be zero-padded. Amplification uses uniformly bounded partial sums. Trace-norm convergent Kraus series defines a state and preserves the opposite partial trace; the producer lemma proves this by bounded cyclicity and a summable nuclear-tail limit. Grouped outcome effects pair through the partial trace. Zero-probability positive branches have trace zero and vanish; only positive branches are normalized. Contractive partial trace permits averaging in trace norm. AC is retained for general sharp local laws. No relativistic or apparatus causality claim is made. Current measurement positive-tail inference is sound; historical unbound reader finding is recorded separately.

citations.quote:
Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited position-outcome law. In
the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}),\,\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})}+\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}),\,\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for a
declared composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned
spaces $H,K$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited suppliers. Let $\rho,\rho'\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be
preparations with reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$,
$\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ and
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$. Then:

**(a) Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of
subsystem $A$ with local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{A}\,E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B),$$
where $E_{A}$ is the spectral projection valued measure of $A$. In particular
the local statistics of subsystem $A$ depend on the composite preparation only
through its reduced preparation, and if $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$ then every local
readout law is the same in $\rho$ and in $\rho'$.

**(b) Determination of the reduced preparation.** Conversely, if
$\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$, then there are a bounded assigned sharp observable
$(P,1)$ of subsystem $A$ and a Borel set $B$ with
$\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)\ne\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)$: the
family of local readout laws of subsystem $A$ determines $\rho_{A}$ among the
preparations of the composite.

**(c) Ideal local measurement.** Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ be a declared
ideal sharp measurement of subsystem $A$
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (a)). Then $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})_{a\in A_{0}}$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement of the declared composite, its outcome probabilities in a
preparation $\rho$ are
$$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a}),$$
and for $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state
$\rho_{a}:=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ of the
composite has the reduced preparation
$$(\rho_{a})_{A}=\frac{P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
which is the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$ by $P_{a}$. The
discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$
has reduced preparations
$$\Phi(\rho)_{A}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a},\qquad \Phi(\rho)_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{B} .$$
The analogous statements hold with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the readings of the cited items and of the cited mathematics. They concern
the declared composite and its declared measurements; they assert no dynamics,
no interaction, no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes
and no empirical fact, and clause (c) is a statement about the declared ideal
Lueders instrument only, not about every laboratory procedure.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: [Unit norm and reduced weight] Put $q_j=\kappa(\psi_j\otimes e_j)$, $\alpha=1/\sqrt2$ and $\beta=e^{i\varphi}/\sqrt2$. By [F4], $\|q_j\|=1$ and $\langle q_1,q_2\rangle=\langle\psi_1,\psi_2\rangle\langle e_1,e_2\rangle=0$, so $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^2=|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$. Thus $I=\mathbb R$ and $\rho(\varphi)=T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}$ by [F1]. Expanding by the sesquilinearity in [F4] gives $T_{\Psi,\Psi}=|\alpha|^2T_{q_1,q_1}+|\beta|^2T_{q_2,q_2}+\alpha\overline\beta T_{q_1,q_2}+\overline\alpha\beta T_{q_2,q_1}$. Applying [F2] termwise gives $\rho(\varphi)_A=\frac12T_{\psi_1,\psi_1}+\frac12T_{\psi_2,\psi_2}+\frac12e^{-i\varphi}\langle e_1,e_2\rangle T_{\psi_1,\psi_2}+\frac12e^{i\varphi}\langle e_2,e_1\rangle T_{\psi_2,\psi_1}$. This proves (a) and the reduction identity for every spin label, without applying a scalar-$L^2$ supplier to vector-valued paths.

[Detection law] By [F3], $p(\varphi)(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)_{A}G(B))$; since $G(B)$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator with $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ and $T_{x,y}$ pairs as $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,y}G(B))=\langle G(B)x,y\rangle$ by [F4], the weight of step 1.1 gives $p(\varphi)(B)=\frac12p_{1}(B)+\frac12p_{2}(B)+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B))$, which is (b).

[Cross-term contraction] Since $G(B)=G(B)^*=G(B)^2$, $\langle G(B)\psi_1,\psi_2\rangle=\langle G(B)\psi_1,G(B)\psi_2\rangle$. By [F5] its modulus is at most $\sqrt{p_1(B)p_2(B)}$. Hence step 2.1 gives $|p(\varphi)(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)|\le|\gamma(B)|\le|\langle e_1,e_2\rangle|\sqrt{p_1(B)p_2(B)}\le|\langle e_1,e_2\rangle|p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$, where the last inequality follows from $(\sqrt{p_1}-\sqrt{p_2})^2\ge0$. The marker overlap is at most one by [F5] and unit normalization. If it is zero, $\gamma(B)=0$ and the detection law is $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ for every phase. This proves (c), including zero-weight bins.

[Visibility] Write $\gamma(B)=|\gamma(B)|e^{i\theta}$ when $\gamma(B)\ne0$; then $\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B))=|\gamma(B)|\cos(\theta-\varphi)$, whose supremum over $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ is $|\gamma(B)|$ (attained at $\varphi=\theta$) and whose infimum is $-|\gamma(B)|$ (attained at $\varphi=\theta+\pi$); when $\gamma(B)=0$ the function is identically zero and the same formulae hold. Hence $\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|$ and $\inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|$, and if $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$ the definition of the visibility gives $V(B)=|\gamma(B)|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$; the bound $V(B)\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|$ is step 3.1. This is (d), and (e) is the special case $|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$ using the ratio bound of step 3.1 and the case $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$.

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 3.1 is (c), step 4.1 is (d), (e); only the declared model, its overlap-normalized hypothesis and the cited mathematics were used, with no measured pattern, count or mechanism asserted, which is (f).

Amended scalar-L2 supplier application: step 1.1 now derives unit norm and reduced operator by a finite rank-one expansion on the actual vector-valued H_s, using exact partial-trace clause (c).
