Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}=0$ when two of $i,j,k$ coincide, and otherwise $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$; the sum ranges over $k\in\{x,y,z\}$. The same convention with indices $1,2,3$ uses the order-preserving relabelling $(1,2,3)=(x,y,z)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume
the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the
outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a
unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint
matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. For every unit $n$, read
$(S_{n},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable under P2. Put
$S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ and, for its outcome-law claim in
(b), read $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ as an assigned sharp observable
under P2. Then:

(a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum
$\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each
$m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the
fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix
$n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$,
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$
and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$;

(b) the Casimir operator $S^{2}$ equals $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as a bounded
operator, so for every preparation $\rho$ the law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ is the Dirac law at
$\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, and one has the
commutation relations
$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and
$[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$ on $H_{s}$, componentwise on the internal factor;

(c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has
$$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$
where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular,
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and
each number lies in $[0,1]$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and
P6, the sharp-observable assignments stated above and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal
factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no
measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components,
no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements
do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement,
and they contain no comparison with data.

Let $s,t\in\frac12\mathbb N$, write $L_s:=\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$ and $L_t:=\{-t,-t+1,\dots,t\}$, and let
$(V_s,J^{(s)}_x,J^{(s)}_y,J^{(s)}_z)$ and $(V_t,J^{(t)}_x,J^{(t)}_y,J^{(t)}_z)$ be the spin models of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] with orthonormal bases $(e^{(s)}_m)_{m\in L_s}$ and
$(e^{(t)}_n)_{n\in L_t}$ and the ladders $J^{(s)}_\pm:=J^{(s)}_x\pm iJ^{(s)}_y$,
$J^{(t)}_\pm:=J^{(t)}_x\pm iJ^{(t)}_y$ and Casimirs $J^{(s)2}$, $J^{(t)2}$
([[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]]). On the tensor product $V_s\otimes V_t$ put

$$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_i:=J^{(s)}_i\otimes I_{V_t}+I_{V_s}\otimes J^{(t)}_i\quad(i=x,y,z),\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}}_\pm:=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x\pm iJ^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z)^2 .$$

Then:

(a) each $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_i$ is self-adjoint, the triple $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$
satisfies the commutation relations of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]], and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=J^{(s)2}\otimes I_{V_t}+I_{V_s}\otimes J^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i}J^{(s)}_i\otimes J^{(t)}_i$ is
self-adjoint and commutes with $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$;

(b) there is an orthogonal decomposition $V_s\otimes V_t=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_j$ into
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}$-invariant subspaces, one for each $j\in\{|s-t|,|s-t|+1,\dots,s+t\}$, with
$\dim W_j=2j+1$, on each of which $(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z)$ is unitarily
equivalent to the spin-$j$ model of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; consequently
$\sum_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}(2j+1)=(2s+1)(2t+1)$;

(c) for every $M\in\frac12\mathbb Z$ the $M$-eigenspace of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$ has dimension
$$N(M):=\#\{m\in L_s:\ M-m\in L_t\}=\begin{cases}\max\bigl(0,\ \min(s,M+t)-\max(-s,M-t)+1\bigr),&M-(s+t)\in\mathbb Z,\\0,&M-(s+t)\notin\mathbb Z.\end{cases},$$
and the identity $(e^{(s)}_m\otimes e^{(t)}_n)_{m,n}$ is an orthonormal basis of $V_s\otimes V_t$ consisting of
eigenvectors of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$ with eigenvalues $m+n$;

(d) the number of summands with parameter equal to $M$ in the decomposition of (b) is
$N(M)-N(M+1)$ if $M\ge0$, and this number equals $1$ when $M-(s+t)\in\mathbb Z$ and $|s-t|\le M\le s+t$, and equals $0$ otherwise; hence the
multiset of parameters in (b) is exactly $\{|s-t|,|s-t|+1,\dots,s+t\}$, each occurring once;

(e) for each $j\in\{|s-t|,\dots,s+t\}$ the space of vectors of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$-eigenvalue $j$ orthogonal to
all summands $W_{j'}$ with $j'>j$ is one-dimensional; for a unit vector $u_j$ in it the vectors
$$v_{j,k}:=\bigl(k!(2j)(2j-1)\cdots(2j-k+1)\bigr)^{-1/2}(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-)^ku_j\qquad(0\le k\le2j)$$
form an orthonormal basis of $W_j$ with $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_zv_{j,k}=(j-k)v_{j,k}$,
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_+v_{j,k}=\sqrt{k(2j-k+1)}\,v_{j,k-1}$ and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-v_{j,k}=\sqrt{(k+1)(2j-k)}\,v_{j,k+1}$; the coefficients of $v_{j,k}$ in the product basis
are therefore determined by the phase of $u_j$, and choosing that phase fixes the Clebsch-Gordan numbers
explicitly; in particular $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_s\otimes e^{(t)}_t$ is a permissible choice.

The theorem is a purely mathematical statement about tensor products of the explicit matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; it asserts no physical coupling, conservation law or
measurement fact.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The adopted composite
reading also carries the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for its
local spectral readouts; the Schmidt and partial-trace deductions below use
only Countable Choice. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ satisfy
$\|\Psi\|=1$, let
$$\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K),\qquad \rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),\qquad \rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$$
be the pure preparation of the declared composite and its two reduced
preparations. Then:

**(a) Schmidt expansion and reductions.** There are an at most countable index
set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq H$,
$(u_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq K$ and numbers $s_{r}>0$ with
$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\,\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})\quad\text{(norm convergence)},\qquad \sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}=1,$$
and the reduced preparations are given by the trace-norm convergent series
$$\rho_{A}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{v_{r},v_{r}},\qquad \rho_{B}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{u_{r},u_{r}} .$$
Moreover $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{4}$.

**(b) Purity and product criterion.** The following are equivalent:
(i) exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero; (ii) $\rho_{A}$ is pure, that is
$\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$; (iii) $\rho_{B}$ is pure;
(iv) $\Psi$ is a product vector, $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$; (v) $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$; (vi) $\rho$ is separable in the trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). In that case
$s_{r_{0}}=1$ at the unique nonzero index and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$,
$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ for $u=v_{r_{0}}$, $v=u_{r_{0}}$.

**(c) Non-product pure preparations.** If $\Psi$ is not a product vector, then
at least two coefficients $s_{r}$ are nonzero, $\rho_{A}$ and $\rho_{B}$ are
mixed, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$, and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$;
the pure preparation is entangled in the full trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). More precisely, if $m=\max_rs_r^2<1$, every separable $\sigma$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma\rho)\le m$ and $\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\ge1-m>0$.

**(d) Scope.** The statement concerns the declared composite, its pure
preparations and the reduced preparations of the factors. It asserts no
dynamics, no interaction, no measurement, no apparatus realization and no
empirical fact; and it concerns pure composite preparations only, mixed-state
separability being outside its scope.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Adopt the framework's composition and measurement readings for a declared
composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the local
sharp-readout law used below. Let $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be a preparation of the
declared composite with reduced preparations
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$, and
let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ be a declared finite or
countable instrument of subsystem $B$, normalized:
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{K}$ in the strong sense, with effects
$F_{a}:=\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ and outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$. Then:
 
**(a) The local extension.** The family
$(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ is a declared
finite or countable instrument of the declared composite, with outcome effects
$F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}=I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$, outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}})$, and conditional states
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0).$$

**(b) No-signalling.** The discarded-outcome state
$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a,r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$
is a preparation of the composite, its reduced preparation on $A$ is unchanged,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho=\rho_{A},$$
and consequently every local outcome law of subsystem $A$ is unchanged:
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\Phi(\rho)}=\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}\qquad\text{for every assigned sharp observable }(A,u_{A})\text{ of }A .$$
The same holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(c) Conditional reductions.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state $\rho_{a}$
has reduced preparation $(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho_{a}$ on $A$,
and
$$\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\,(\rho_{a})_{A}=\rho_{A};$$
the conditional reduced preparations $(\rho_{a})_{A}$ may differ from
$\rho_{A}$, and the recorded outcome $a$ is the classical datum needed to
select them.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the stated readings and of the cited mathematics; they concern declared
instruments of the declared composite. They assert no relativistic causality
principle, no claim that a particular apparatus realizes the declared
instrument, no disturbance of the other factor by any concrete device and no
empirical fact.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}=0$ when two of $i,j,k$ coincide, and otherwise $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$; the sum ranges over $k\in\{x,y,z\}$. The same convention with indices $1,2,3$ uses the order-preserving relabelling $(1,2,3)=(x,y,z)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

derivations.claim: [Singlet data and reduced preparations] The basis actions of the Pauli matrices are $\sigma_xe_+=e_-$, $\sigma_xe_-=e_+$, $\sigma_ye_+=ie_-$, $\sigma_ye_-=-ie_+$, $\sigma_ze_+=e_+$, and $\sigma_ze_-=-e_-$. On each of the two terms $e_+\otimes e_-$ and $e_-\otimes e_+$, the $z$-component $\sigma_z\otimes I+I\otimes\sigma_z$ vanishes; applying the displayed $x$- and $y$-actions shows respectively that $(\sigma_x\otimes I+I\otimes\sigma_x)(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)=0$ and $(\sigma_y\otimes I+I\otimes\sigma_y)(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)=0$. Since $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\sigma_i\otimes I+I\otimes\sigma_i)$, this proves $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}\Psi=0$ for all three indices. Orthonormality makes $\Psi$ unit; the partial-trace formula [F4] gives $\rho_A=\frac12T_{e_+,e_+}+\frac12T_{e_-,e_-}=\frac12I$ and $\rho_B=\frac12I$, with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_A^2=\frac12$. The two positive Schmidt coefficients show $\Psi$ is not product. This is (a).

[The declared joint PVM] For each unit $a$, the two operators $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ are orthogonal projections with sum $I_V$ by [F2]; likewise for $b$. By [F3], each $G_{a,b}(\{(\varepsilon,\delta)\})=P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta}$ is an orthogonal projection. The tensor product rule shows distinct outcome pairs give orthogonal projections, and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}G_{a,b}(\{(\varepsilon,\delta)\})=(\sum_\varepsilon P_{a,\varepsilon})\otimes(\sum_\delta P_{b,\delta})=I_V\otimes I_V$. Thus $G_{a,b}$ is a finite PVM, hence a declared ideal sharp joint measurement under P3.

Fix unit $a$ and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $(u_+,u_-)$ of $a\cdot\sigma$, with eigenvalues $+1,-1$. Write its two columns in the fixed basis $(e_+,e_-)$ as the unitary matrix $W$ and set $\Delta=\det W$. Expanding the two elementary tensors gives $\kappa(u_+\otimes u_-)-\kappa(u_-\otimes u_+)=\Delta[\kappa(e_+\otimes e_-)-\kappa(e_-\otimes e_+)]$. Orthonormality gives $|\Delta|^2=\|u_+\|^2\|u_-\|^2-|\langle u_+,u_-\rangle|^2=1$, by direct two-coordinate expansion. Thus with $\eta=\Delta^{-1}$, the fixed vector is $\Psi=\eta[\kappa(u_+\otimes u_-)-\kappa(u_-\otimes u_+)]/\sqrt2$, where $|\eta|=1$. For unit $b$ use $P_{b,\pm}=(I\pm b\cdot\sigma)/2$ from [F2]. This phase changes no projection norm or probability.

[Joint outcome probabilities] By step 1.3, $(P_{a,+}\otimes P_{b,+})\Psi=\eta\kappa(u_+\otimes P_{b,+}u_-)/\sqrt2$. Since $|\eta|=1$, [F5] and [F2] give $p(+,+)=\|P_{b,+}u_-\|^2/2=[1+\langle(b\cdot\sigma)u_-,u_-\rangle]/4$. The Pauli identities [F1] give $(a\cdot\sigma)(b\cdot\sigma)+(b\cdot\sigma)(a\cdot\sigma)=2(a\cdot b)I$. Pairing this identity against $u_-$ and using self-adjointness and $(a\cdot\sigma)u_-=-u_-$ gives $\langle(b\cdot\sigma)u_-,u_-\rangle=-a\cdot b$; the same calculation for $u_+$ gives $+a\cdot b$. Applying the other three projection pairs therefore gives $p(+,+)=p(-,-)=(1-a\cdot b)/4=\sin^2(\theta/2)/2$ and $p(+,-)=p(-,+)=(1+a\cdot b)/4=\cos^2(\theta/2)/2$, where $\cos\theta=a\cdot b$. These nonnegative numbers sum to one, proving (b).

[Correlation and marginals] Summing with the product signs, $\mathbb E(a,b)=p(+,+)+p(-,-)-p(+,-)-p(-,+)=\frac12\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}+\frac12\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac12\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac12\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}=\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}=-\cos\theta$, which is (c) since $\theta$ is the angle between $a$ and $b$; the marginals are $p_{A}(+)=p(+,+)+p(+,-)=\frac12$ and $p_{A}(-)=\frac12$, and likewise $p_{B}(\pm)=\frac12$, independent of the other direction. The preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\frac12I$ are unchanged by a discarded local instrument on the other factor by [F6]; this is (d).

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 3.1 is (c), (d); only the declared internal-factor composite and the cited mathematics were used. No spatial, temporal, relativistic, concrete-apparatus or empirical input enters, which is (e).

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(D,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space, let $L^2(D,\mu)$ denote the quotient of square-integrable measurable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), let $K$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with unit vectors $e_1,e_2$, let $a,b\in L^2(D,\mu)$ be unit vectors, and let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$ with $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$. Choose measurable representatives of $a,b$; all displayed pointwise expressions are understood almost everywhere, and the integrals below are independent of the representatives. Put

$$\Psi:=\alpha\,a\otimes e_1+\beta\,b\otimes e_2\in L^2(D)\widehat\otimes K .$$

Then:

(a) the reduced positive trace-class weight $\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ on $L^2(D)$ is

$$\rho=|\alpha|^2T_{a,a}+|\beta|^2T_{b,b}+\alpha\overline\beta\,\langle e_1,e_2\rangle\,T_{a,b}+\overline\alpha\beta\,\langle e_2,e_1\rangle\,T_{b,a};$$

(b) for every measurable $B\subseteq D$ with finite measure, writing $P_B$ for the multiplication operator by $\mathbf 1_B$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_B)=\int_B\Bigl(|\alpha|^2|a|^2+|\beta|^2|b|^2+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha\overline\beta\langle e_1,e_2\rangle\,a(x)\overline{b(x)}\bigr)\Bigr)d\mu ;$$

(c) the marker overlap contracts the cross term: $|\langle e_1,e_2\rangle|\le1$, and if $e_1\perp e_2$ the cross term in (b) vanishes, leaving the incoherent weight $|\alpha|^2|a|^2+|\beta|^2|b|^2$.

The weight satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\|\Psi\|^2=1+2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline\beta\langle a,b\rangle\langle e_1,e_2\rangle)$; it is a density operator precisely when $\|\Psi\|=1$. The stated assumptions do not force this normalization. These are identities for the specified vector and its unnormalized weight; they assert no measured detector law and cover no selective conditioning.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited position-outcome law. In
the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}),\,\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})}+\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}),\,\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.

Adopt the declared marked two-component model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] with unit path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, unit marker states $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
phase family $\rho(\varphi)$, marker-carried which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$, and a declared detection bin $B$. Assume the model is
**overlap-normalized**, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the
cited position and local-readout suppliers. Put
$$\gamma(B):=\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\,\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle,\qquad p_{j}(B):=\langle G(B)\psi_{j},\psi_{j}\rangle\quad(j=1,2),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(p_{1}(B)+p_{2}(B)\bigr).$$
Then:
 
**(a) Unit-norm phase family.** $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every $\varphi$, so
$\rho(\varphi)=T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}$.
 
**(b) Detection law.** For every $\varphi$,
$$p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B)\bigr).$$
 
**(c) Contraction of the cross term.** For every $\varphi$,
$$\bigl|p(\varphi)(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)\bigr|\le|\gamma(B)|\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\sqrt{p_{1}(B)p_{2}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B).$$
In particular, if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$
for every $\varphi$: the marked detection law is exactly the which-path law.
 
**(d) Visibility.** Writing $\gamma(B)=|\gamma(B)|e^{i\theta}$ with
$\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, one has
$$\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|,\qquad \inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|,$$
so that, whenever $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$, the fringe visibility of clause (e)
of the definition is
$$V(B)=\frac{|\gamma(B)|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle| .$$
 
**(e) Extremes.** If the model is trivially marked,
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$, then for every bin with
$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$ one has
$V(B)=\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le1$;
if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $V(B)=0$ for every bin with $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$.
 
**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional computations in the declared
model. They assert no measured pattern, no trial counts, no statistical
analysis, no decoherence mechanism, no irreversibility and no which-path
ontology, and they contain no empirical claim.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: [Profile integrals] Fubini [L3] factors each three-dimensional integral into its longitudinal integral and $\|\eta\|^2=1$. Since $|f_j|^2=\ell^{-1}\mathbf1_{[0,\ell]}$ almost everywhere, $\|\psi_j\|^2=\ell^{-1}\int_0^\ell dx_1=1$. The longitudinal sign change gives $\langle\psi_1,\psi_2\rangle=\ell^{-1}(\int_0^{\ell/2}dx_1-\int_{\ell/2}^{\ell}dx_1)=0$. On $B$ both profiles agree, so $p_1(B)=p_2(B)=\langle G(B)\psi_1,\psi_2\rangle=\ell^{-1}\int_0^{\ell/2}dx_1=1/2$. The integrands are integrable because they are bounded longitudinal profiles of finite support times $|\eta|^2\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$. This proves the path unit norm and orthogonality in (i), and the data in (ii).

[Detection law and visibility] By step 1.1 the model is overlap-normalized; the marker theorem clause (a) in [L2] then gives $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every real phase and hence $I=\mathbb R$, so [L1] and [L2] apply with $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\frac12$ and $\gamma(B)=\cos\vartheta\cdot\frac12$; hence $p(\varphi)(B)=\frac12+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\frac{\cos\vartheta}{2})=\frac12(1+\cos\vartheta\cos\varphi)$ and $V(B)=|\gamma(B)|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\frac{\cos\vartheta/2}{1/2}=\cos\vartheta$, which is (ii); at $\vartheta=0$ and $\vartheta=\pi/2$ the displayed laws and values are the ones of (iii).
[Assembly] Step 1.1 is (i), step 2.1 is (ii) and (iii); only the declared model and the cited mathematics were used, so no measured pattern, count or apparatus response is asserted.

boundaries.reason: The declared bin has p_1(B)=p_2(B)=1/2>0, so no empty-bin case arises in the example.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 evaluates the orthogonal-marker case ϑ=π/2 with vanishing cross term, and step 1.1 the orthogonality of the path components.
Step 1.1 computes the unit norms of the profiles and step 2.1 the visibility one at ϑ=0.

boundaries.reason: The flat profiles and the declared bin carry no degeneracy; the marker states are distinct and the profile supports are as declared.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 evaluates the endpoint values ϑ=0 and ϑ=π/2 of the declared interval [0,π/2].
Steps 1.1 and 2.1 use the marked model and its contraction theorem, whose hypothesis includes the Axiom of Countable Choice.

The example states identities, not a biconditional.

risk_review.notes: Checked all three verification steps and exact Fubini, marked-model and corrected visibility suppliers. Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite and the integrands factor as bounded compactly supported profiles times |eta|^2 in L1. Shared cell endpoints are null, so norms are one, cross overlap zero and each bin weight/cross pairing is 1/2 even though B has infinite volume. The scalar marker supplier is used only for normalization/reduction, not its finite-measure pointwise bin clause. p_mix=1/2 is positive, so V=cos vartheta is defined; endpoints 0 and pi/2 give contrast one and zero. Choice is carried from position/visibility laws. Flat profiles are L2 idealizations, with no kinetic-domain/dynamical or observed-data assertion.

citations.quote:
Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for the
internal factors of two declared spin-half particles
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited
spin-outcome spectral construction. Let
$V=\mathbb C^{2}$ be a declared spin-half internal factor with orthonormal
basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and spin matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], so that
$S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and for each unit vector
$n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ let $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. On the declared
composite of the two internal factors $V\widehat\otimes V$, define the total
spin component for each $i\in\{x,y,z\}$ by
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=S_i\otimes I_V+I_V\otimes S_i.$$
For a unit direction $n$ the local spin observable is
$S_{n}\otimes I_V$ or $I_V\otimes S_n$, read as a bounded assigned sharp
observable of its factor with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$
([[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Put
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr),\qquad \rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(V\widehat\otimes V),$$
the **singlet preparation**, and let $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho$,
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}\rho$ be its reduced preparations. Then:
 
**(a) Singlet data.** $\Psi$ is a unit vector; $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for
all $i$; $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$; and the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$
is $\Psi=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$
with two equal coefficients, so $\Psi$ is not a product vector and both
reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\tfrac12$.
 
**(b) Joint directional laws.** For unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$\theta:=\arccos(a\cdot b)\in[0,\pi]$, put
$P_{n,\varepsilon}=\frac12(I+\varepsilon n\cdot\sigma)$ for
$\varepsilon\in\{-1,+1\}$. These are the spectral projections of $S_n$.
Define the four-outcome joint PVM on the power set of $\{-1,+1\}^{2}$ by
$$G_{a,b}(C):=\sum_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in C}P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta}\qquad(C\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{2}).$$
The declared PVM is the ideal joint model readout for the two factors; its
P2 outcome probabilities
$p(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho G_{a,b}(\{(\varepsilon,\delta)\})\bigr)$ are
$$p(+,+)=p(-,-)=\tfrac12\sin^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},\qquad p(+,-)=p(-,+)=\tfrac12\cos^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},$$
where the first sign refers to the outcome $+\hbar/2$ or $-\hbar/2$ of
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and the second to that of $I\otimes S_{b}$;
in particular the four numbers are nonnegative and sum to one.
 
**(c) Correlation function.** With the product $\varepsilon\delta$ of the two
sign labels,
$$\mathbb E(a,b):=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,+1\}}\varepsilon\delta\,p(\varepsilon,\delta)=-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b .$$
In particular $\mathbb E(a,a)=-1$ and $\mathbb E(a,-a)=+1$: the outcomes are
perfectly anti-correlated for equal directions.
 
**(d) Setting-independent marginals.** The marginal laws are
$p_{A}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ and $p_{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$, independent of $b$ and of
$a$ respectively; the reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$ are
unchanged under the other factor's declared ideal local measurement model
followed by discarding its record, in agreement with
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b).
 
**(e) Scope.** This is a thought experiment of the declared framework: the
composite is an internal-factor composite, and the PVM and probabilities in
clause (b) are ideal model objects and predictions under P2. The particles are
not assigned spatial positions or worldlines here; no spatial separation,
temporal order, relativistic consideration, concrete apparatus, performed
measurement, recorded data or empirical correlation enters. The computation
draws no conclusion about nature and makes no claim about the completeness of
the framework or about any hidden-variable model.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}=0$ when two of $i,j,k$ coincide, and otherwise $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$; the sum ranges over $k\in\{x,y,z\}$. The same convention with indices $1,2,3$ uses the order-preserving relabelling $(1,2,3)=(x,y,z)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for a
declared composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned
spaces $H,K$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited suppliers. Let $\rho,\rho'\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be
preparations with reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$,
$\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ and
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$. Then:

**(a) Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of
subsystem $A$ with local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{A}\,E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B),$$
where $E_{A}$ is the spectral projection valued measure of $A$. In particular
the local statistics of subsystem $A$ depend on the composite preparation only
through its reduced preparation, and if $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$ then every local
readout law is the same in $\rho$ and in $\rho'$.

**(b) Determination of the reduced preparation.** Conversely, if
$\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$, then there are a bounded assigned sharp observable
$(P,1)$ of subsystem $A$ and a Borel set $B$ with
$\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)\ne\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)$: the
family of local readout laws of subsystem $A$ determines $\rho_{A}$ among the
preparations of the composite.

**(c) Ideal local measurement.** Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ be a declared
ideal sharp measurement of subsystem $A$
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (a)). Then $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})_{a\in A_{0}}$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement of the declared composite, its outcome probabilities in a
preparation $\rho$ are
$$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a}),$$
and for $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state
$\rho_{a}:=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ of the
composite has the reduced preparation
$$(\rho_{a})_{A}=\frac{P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
which is the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$ by $P_{a}$. The
discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$
has reduced preparations
$$\Phi(\rho)_{A}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a},\qquad \Phi(\rho)_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{B} .$$
The analogous statements hold with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the readings of the cited items and of the cited mathematics. They concern
the declared composite and its declared measurements; they assert no dynamics,
no interaction, no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes
and no empirical fact, and clause (c) is a statement about the declared ideal
Lueders instrument only, not about every laboratory procedure.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Density operators are
the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators of trace one
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]]), and for $u,u'\in H$, $v,v'\in K$ the rank-one
operator $T_{u\otimes v,\,u'\otimes v'}$ is the one of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]].

**(a) Product vectors and pure product states.** A vector $\Psi\in
H\widehat\otimes K$ is a **product vector** when $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
some $u\in H$, $v\in K$. A **pure product state** of the composite is a
density operator of the form
$$T_{\Psi,\Psi},\qquad \Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v),\quad \|u\|=\|v\|=1 .$$
A vector is **non-product** when it is not a product vector.

**(b) Separable states.** Write $\mathcal P$ for the set of all pure product
states, a subset of the set $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of density operators. The
**separable states** are the elements of the trace-norm closed convex hull
$$\mathcal S(H,K):=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\,\mathcal P \ \subseteq\ D(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
where $\operatorname{conv}$ denotes the set of finite convex combinations and
the closure is taken in the trace norm $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ of
[[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. A state
$\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is **entangled** (with respect to the
declared splitting $H,K$) when $\rho\notin\mathcal S(H,K)$.

**(c) Conventions and elementary consequences of the form of the definition.**
The set $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ consists exactly of the finite sums
$\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_{j}T_{\Psi_{j},\Psi_{j}}$ with $n\ge1$, weights $w_{j}\ge0$,
$\sum_{j}w_{j}=1$ and unit product vectors $\Psi_{j}$: such sums are convex
combinations of density operators and hence density operators
([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]] clause (a)),
without any orthogonality requirement on the product vectors.
Every element of $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is a density operator, and
$\mathcal S(H,K)$ is a convex subset of $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$: if $\rho,\sigma$
are limits of convex combinations $\rho_{n}\to\rho$, $\sigma_{n}\to\sigma$ and
$t\in[0,1]$, then $t\rho+(1-t)\sigma$ is the trace-norm limit of the convex
combinations $t\rho_{n}+(1-t)\sigma_{n}$. Separability of a state is a
property of the declared splitting $(H,K)$; no assertion is made here about
its behaviour under a different factorization of a larger space.

**(d) Finite dimension.** When $H$ and $K$ are finite dimensional,
$\mathcal P$ is compact and $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is already closed
in the trace norm (it is a compact, hence closed, convex set in the
finite-dimensional space of endomorphisms of $H\widehat\otimes K$), so
$\mathcal S(H,K)=\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ and no closure convention is
needed. In the general case the closure in clause (b) is declared explicitly
and is part of the definition.

**(e) Pure-state specialization and status.** A pure state $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\|\Psi\|=1$ is separable in the precise trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of clause (b) exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector of clause (a); otherwise it is entangled. This is the proved mathematical specialization of [[lem-nrqm-composites-pure-state-separability-criterion]], whose locally defined $\mathcal P,\mathcal S$ are exactly those above. Clauses (a)-(e) fix mathematical vocabulary and adopt no physical assumption, dynamics, measurement or probability law. Whether a laboratory preparation realizes a separable or entangled state for the declared splitting remains a tested identification with uncertainty, not a consequence about nature of this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.
