Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],
   [[def-metric-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for the
internal factors of two declared spin-half particles
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited
spin-outcome spectral construction. Let
$V=\mathbb C^{2}$ be a declared spin-half internal factor with orthonormal
basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and spin matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], so that
$S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and for each unit vector
$n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ let $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. On the declared
composite of the two internal factors $V\widehat\otimes V$, define the total
spin component for each $i\in\{x,y,z\}$ by
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=S_i\otimes I_V+I_V\otimes S_i.$$
For a unit direction $n$ the local spin observable is
$S_{n}\otimes I_V$ or $I_V\otimes S_n$, read as a bounded assigned sharp
observable of its factor with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$
([[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Put
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr),\qquad \rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(V\widehat\otimes V),$$
the **singlet preparation**, and let $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho$,
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}\rho$ be its reduced preparations. Then:
 
**(a) Singlet data.** $\Psi$ is a unit vector; $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for
all $i$; $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$; and the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$
is $\Psi=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$
with two equal coefficients, so $\Psi$ is not a product vector and both
reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\tfrac12$.
 
**(b) Joint directional laws.** For unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$\theta:=\arccos(a\cdot b)\in[0,\pi]$, put
$P_{n,\varepsilon}=\frac12(I+\varepsilon n\cdot\sigma)$ for
$\varepsilon\in\{-1,+1\}$. These are the spectral projections of $S_n$.
Define the four-outcome joint PVM on the power set of $\{-1,+1\}^{2}$ by
$$G_{a,b}(C):=\sum_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in C}P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta}\qquad(C\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{2}).$$
The declared PVM is the ideal joint model readout for the two factors; its
P2 outcome probabilities
$p(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho G_{a,b}(\{(\varepsilon,\delta)\})\bigr)$ are
$$p(+,+)=p(-,-)=\tfrac12\sin^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},\qquad p(+,-)=p(-,+)=\tfrac12\cos^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},$$
where the first sign refers to the outcome $+\hbar/2$ or $-\hbar/2$ of
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and the second to that of $I\otimes S_{b}$;
in particular the four numbers are nonnegative and sum to one.
 
**(c) Correlation function.** With the product $\varepsilon\delta$ of the two
sign labels,
$$\mathbb E(a,b):=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,+1\}}\varepsilon\delta\,p(\varepsilon,\delta)=-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b .$$
In particular $\mathbb E(a,a)=-1$ and $\mathbb E(a,-a)=+1$: the outcomes are
perfectly anti-correlated for equal directions.
 
**(d) Setting-independent marginals.** The marginal laws are
$p_{A}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ and $p_{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$, independent of $b$ and of
$a$ respectively; the reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$ are
unchanged under the other factor's declared ideal local measurement model
followed by discarding its record, in agreement with
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b).
 
**(e) Scope.** This is a thought experiment of the declared framework: the
composite is an internal-factor composite, and the PVM and probabilities in
clause (b) are ideal model objects and predictions under P2. The particles are
not assigned spatial positions or worldlines here; no spatial separation,
temporal order, relativistic consideration, concrete apparatus, performed
measurement, recorded data or empirical correlation enters. The computation
draws no conclusion about nature and makes no claim about the completeness of
the framework or about any hidden-variable model.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited
spectral-law supplier. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$
be a unit vector, $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ the associated pure preparation, and
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ its
reduced preparations. Then:

**(a) Product preparations factorize.** If $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$, then for every bounded effect $F$ on $H$ and every bounded
effect $F'$ on $K$
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(F\otimes F')\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}F)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F').$$
In particular, for a declared finite-outcome measurement of $A$ with effect
family $(F_{i})$ and one of $B$ with $(F'_{j})$, the joint outcome
probabilities factorize, $p(i,j)=p_{A}(i)p_{B}(j)$: in a product preparation
the two subsystems have independent local statistics.

**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=0\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$
so the joint law of the corresponding two-outcome local measurements does not
factorize; the product of the marginal probabilities exceeds the joint
probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$.

**(c) Scope.** The statement is a conditional computation for pure
preparations of the declared composite; it asserts no dynamics, no
interaction, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no
empirical fact, and it does not claim that a joint law failing to factorize
establishes any particular physical mechanism.

derivations.claim: [Marginals] By [L2], $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},e_{+}\otimes e_{-}}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},e_{-}\otimes e_{+}}=T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$, so the linearity of the partial trace gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\frac12I$; likewise $\operatorname{Tr}_{A}M=\frac12I$. Together with $\rho_{A}=\frac12I$ from [L1] and $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}=\frac12I$ by definition these are the marginal identities in (i). Put $q_1=\kappa(e_+\otimes e_-)$, $q_2=\kappa(e_-\otimes e_+)$; they are orthonormal and $\Psi=(q_1-q_2)/\sqrt2$. Thus the displayed mixture and the rank-one action in [L2] give $M\Psi=\Psi/2$, whereas $\rho\Psi=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\Psi=\Psi$. Since $\Psi$ is unit, $\rho\ne M$, completing (i).

[Correlations of the product mixture] By [L2] and [L4] the joint outcome law of the local measurements of $S_{a}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{b}$ in $M$ is the weighted average of the two product laws, so $\mathbb E_{M}(a,b)=\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle+\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle=\frac12(a_{3})(-b_{3})+\frac12(-a_{3})(b_{3})=-a_{3}b_{3}$; with [L1] this is (ii).

[Local indistinguishability and separability] Let $\tau_B$ be any preparation of $B$. Its density expansion is $\tau_B=\sum_jq_jT_{z_j,z_j}$ in trace norm, with unit $z_j$, $q_j>0$ and $\sum_jq_j=1$, by [L5]. The independent extension of the proper mixture is the trace-norm sum $\Omega=\sum_j(q_j/2)(T_{e_+\otimes z_j,e_+\otimes z_j}+T_{e_-\otimes z_j,e_-\otimes z_j})$: every summand is positive, and its trace norm equals its nonnegative trace, so the series converges with trace one by [L4], [L5]. The rank-one reduction formula [L2] and trace-norm continuity [L5] give $\operatorname{Tr}_B\Omega=(T_{e_+,e_+}+T_{e_-,e_-})/2=I_A/2$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_A\Omega=\tau_B$, which need not equal $I_B/2$. Since $\rho$ and $M$ also have reduction $I_A/2$ by [L1] and step 1.1, [L3] proves all local-$A$ readout laws agree for $\rho$, $M$ and this arbitrary-$B$ extension. The displayed convex decomposition makes $M$ separable by [L4], while $\rho$ is non-product and pure by [L1] and the purity criterion. Their joint laws differ at $(x,x)$ by step 1.2. This proves (iii) and (iv) with the full arbitrary-extension claim.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with $H\widehat\otimes K$ their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). A **product vector** means an elementary tensor $v\otimes u$ with $v\in H$ and $u\in K$. Then for every $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable index set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq H$ and $(u_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq K$, and numbers $s_r>0$ with

$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r\qquad\text{(norm convergence in }H\widehat\otimes K),$$

and $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. The $s_r$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of $CC^*$, where $C:\overline{K_0}\to H_0$ is the linear coefficient operator on countable closed factor supports of $\Psi$, defined below; if $J$ is infinite then $s_r\to0$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ has $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector. No assertion about separability of mixed density operators is made here.

For clarity, choose finite algebraic tensors converging to $\Psi$ and let $H_0\subseteq H$, $K_0\subseteq K$ be the closed spans of their factor vectors. These supports have finite/countable orthonormal bases, and $\Psi\in H_0\widehat\otimes K_0$. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{K_0}$ consists of symbols $\bar z$, with $a\bar z:=\overline{\bar a z}$ and $\langle\bar z,\bar w\rangle_{\overline{K_0}}:=\langle w,z\rangle_{K_0}$. For an orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $K_0$, write $\Psi=\sum_jh_j\otimes f_j$ and set $C\bar f_j=h_j$, extending linearly and continuously. The positive singular values and the nonzero spectrum of $CC^*$ are independent of these supports and bases, as the reduced-state identity proved below shows.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has
   $$\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$$
   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   without assuming that $H$ has a Hilbert basis;
3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace
   norm: for trace-class $S,T$ and scalars $a,b$,
   $\operatorname{tr}(aS+bT)=a\operatorname{tr}(S)+b\operatorname{tr}(T)$ and
   $|\operatorname{tr}(T)|\le\|T\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],
   [[def-metric-space]]).

derivations.claim: [Maximum and the strict gap] By [F2], $\lambda_r>0$ and $\sum_r\lambda_r=1$. Fix one $r_0\in J$ and put $c=\lambda_{r_0}>0$. The set $E=\{r:\lambda_r\ge c\}$ is nonempty and finite: any finite subset of $E$ with $N$ elements has weight sum at least $Nc\le1$, so $E$ has at most $\lfloor1/c\rfloor$ elements. The maximum $m$ on this finite set is a maximum on $J$, since every weight outside $E$ is below $c\le m$. If $\Psi$ is non-product, [F2] gives at least two positive weights; at an index $r_*$ attaining $m$, another positive weight implies $m<\sum_r\lambda_r=1$.

[Finite orthogonal estimates] For an orthonormal family $(e_r)$, a vector $x$ and a finite set $F$, expanding $\|x-\sum_{r\in F}\langle x,e_r\rangle e_r\|^2$ gives $\|x\|^2-\sum_{r\in F}|\langle x,e_r\rangle|^2\ge0$. Thus for unit $a,b$ the sums of $|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2$ and $|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2$ are each at most one, using conjugate symmetry and the supremum of finite sums. For finite complex sequences $(\alpha_r),(\beta_r)$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r|\le(\sum_r|\alpha_r|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)^{1/2}$: this follows by expanding $\sum_r|\alpha_r-t\overline{\beta_r}|^2\ge0$ with $t=(\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r)/(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)$ when the denominator is positive, and is immediate otherwise.

[Exact continuity of the fixed trace witness] For every trace-class $T$ on $L$, [F3] gives $\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)=\langle T\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ and $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)|\le\|T\Psi\|\|\Psi\|\le\|T\|\le\|T\|_1$, since $\|\Psi\|=1$. Applying this estimate to $T-S$ proves $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(SP_\Psi)|\le\|T-S\|_1$. Thus this particular bounded trace functional is 1-Lipschitz; no unspecified continuity theorem or unbounded cyclicity is used. Also $P_\Psi\Psi=\Psi$, so $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=\langle P_\Psi\Psi,\Psi\rangle=1$.

[The overlap bound, with the conjugations fixed] For a finite Schmidt truncation $\Psi_F$, [F1] gives $\langle\Psi_F,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle=\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle\langle u_r,b\rangle$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle a,v_r\rangle\langle b,u_r\rangle$. Applying step 1.2 to $\alpha_r=s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle$ and $\beta_r=\langle u_r,b\rangle$ gives a modulus bound $(\sum_{r\in F}\lambda_r|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_{r\in F}|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2)^{1/2}\le\sqrt m$. The Schmidt truncations converge in norm [F2], so continuity of the Hilbert pairing passes this bound to $\Psi$. At $a=v_{r_*}$ and $b=u_{r_*}$, orthonormality gives overlap $s_{r_*}$ and squared overlap $m$.

[Convex hull and its closure] For unit product $q=\kappa(a\otimes b)$, [F3] and first-linear conjugate symmetry give $\operatorname{tr}(T_{q,q}P_\Psi)=\langle T_{q,q}\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\langle\Psi,q\rangle\langle q,\Psi\rangle=|\langle\Psi,q\rangle|^2\le m$ by step 2.1. Trace linearity gives the same real bound for finite convex combinations. For $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of closure supplies a single $\tau\in\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ with $\|\sigma-\tau\|_1<\varepsilon$. Step 1.3 gives $|\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau P_\Psi)|<\varepsilon$; letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ shows that $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ is real and at most $m$. This neighborhood argument does not select a sequence of approximants.

[Equivalence and distance] If $\Psi$ is non-product, steps 1.1, 1.3 and 3.1 give $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1>m\ge\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ for all $\sigma\in\mathcal S$, so $P_\Psi\notin\mathcal S$. Moreover step 1.3 gives $\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge|\operatorname{tr}((P_\Psi-\sigma)P_\Psi)|=1-\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\ge1-m$. Conversely a unit product vector has $P_\Psi\in\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal S$. If initially $\Psi=\kappa(x\otimes y)$ with arbitrary nonzero factors, [F1] gives $\|x\|\|y\|=1$; therefore $a=x/\|x\|$ and $b=\|x\|y$ are unit and $\Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)$. This proves the full claimed equivalence for the declared trace-norm closure and the strict witness bound.

Unit Schmidt weights are nonempty, summable and positive; a finite threshold set yields an attained maximum, strictly below one for nonproduct vectors.
